commits.message:
perf(hermes-750): fetch Langfuse prompt details concurrently instead of sequentially

app/prompt_runtime/langfuse_prompts.py _refresh_cache() fetched all 38
prompts one HTTP round-trip at a time (N+1 pattern) - measured at ~33s on
a cold cache before this fix. The cache lasts 5 minutes, so this only hit
the first request after expiry, but that request could fail for any
caller with a normal 10-30s timeout even though the fetch would have
succeeded given more time.

Fixed with a ThreadPoolExecutor (stdlib, no new dependency) fetching
prompt details in parallel, default concurrency 8, tunable via
HERMES_LANGFUSE_PROMPT_FETCH_CONCURRENCY without a redeploy. A single
failed detail fetch still only drops that one prompt from the registry,
same as before - it never aborts the whole refresh.

Verified against the live Langfuse instance: 33.59s -> 7.55s for the same
38 prompts, correct prompt_count both times. New check script covers
correctness+timing, that one simulated failure does not abort the batch,
and the env-var concurrency setting (including invalid-value fallback and
clamping to a minimum of 1).

Full regression: HERMES-400 and HERMES-850 checks unaffected. The three
pre-existing HERMES-750/800 check failures (stale Langfuse prompt IDs
from the earlier Portkey-era registry, documented separately in
HERMES-750-litellm-prompt-runtime-foundation.md) are unchanged by this
fix - not a new regression.

fix(hermes-100): close the RBAC gap on /understanding/* and /submissions/evaluate*

Both route groups had no permission dependency wired at all -- confirmed
against the router source and, separately, against live traffic (zero
hits on either path in the last 5000 log lines, and no code anywhere in
jobFynder-BE-nestJS calls out to these endpoints -- the only Hermes<-CORE
integration currently built is the reverse direction, CORE's /hermes/*
controller receiving calls FROM Hermes/agents). Safe to enable: nothing
live was depending on these routes staying open.

Adds require_permission(understanding:parse) to the two parse endpoints
and understanding:parse to the taxonomy write endpoints (normalize,
extract-signals, suggestions), understanding:read to the taxonomy GET
endpoints. Adds submissions:evaluate to POST /submissions/evaluate and
/evaluate/from-handoff specifically -- scoped narrowly to what was
actually documented as the gap; workflow-policy and the tracker/status
extract endpoints are unchanged (out of scope for this fix, not silently
expanded).

Internal callers (channel intake, onboarding, context cards, email
parsing) all call understand_document() as a direct Python import, never
over HTTP -- confirmed via grep before this change, so none of them are
affected by adding auth to the HTTP route.

Provisioned a new jobfynder-core RBAC user (scoped: understanding:parse,
understanding:read, submissions:evaluate) via the existing
hermes-access-control.py script, for when CORE integration actually
starts calling these routes -- token stored at
/root/hermes-token-jobfynder-core.txt, never printed.

Verified live post-deploy: 401 with no token, 403 with a token scoped to
a different permission (n8n automation token), 200 with the new
jobfynder-core token -- including a full parse-text call that correctly
fell back to the LLM via LiteLLM (extract-fast) on low-confidence input.
workflow-policy confirmed still open (unaffected, by design).

fix(hermes-750,800): repoint 3 check scripts at the current prompt registry

hermes-750-prompt-runtime-check.py, hermes-800-foundation-check.py, and
hermes-800-resume-builder-suggestion-check.py all still referenced
resume_builder.summary_improve / resume_builder.bullet_rewrite /
matching.fit_explanation -- prompt IDs retired when the live Langfuse
registry moved to the jf.* naming scheme. hermes-800-foundation-check.py
and hermes-800-resume-builder-suggestion-check.py were a pure rename fix
(app/resume_builder/adapters.py already used jf.resume.summary.generate
and jf.resume.experience.rewrite -- only the test assertions were stale).

hermes-750-prompt-runtime-check.py needed more: the live registry also
moved from raw source_text/target_role/constraints variables to a
Context-Card-based shape (candidate_card/job_card objects,
app/context/models.py), and prompt.domain changed from resume_builder
to resume. Rewrote the dry-run payloads to match the current schema and
empirically verified each assertion against the live registry before
writing it (GET /prompts/jf.resume.summary.generate for the schema, live
POST /prompts/run calls for the positive path, the fabrication-block
path via candidate_card.summary_snippet, and the missing-required-
variables path) rather than guessing at what would pass.

All three verified passing against the live hermes-api container.
feat(hermes-850): add pika dep and graph-consumer service
fix(graph): make app imports stable in service containers
fix(graph): honor tenant subscription lifetime limit
feat: add read-only draft review UI

fix(hermes-850): use constant-time comparison for Graph clientState check

verify_notification_client_state() compared the shared secret with a
plain == , which leaks timing information a network attacker could in
principle use to guess it character-by-character. The public-facing
check (communication/comm_gateway/main.py, the actual front door for
this webhook) already used hmac.compare_digest for exactly this reason
-- this was the one place that had not caught up to match. Low
practical risk today since this is a defense-in-depth re-check behind
a private, credentialed RabbitMQ queue, not the primary boundary, but
free to fix and worth being consistent about.

Found during the Microsoft Graph pipeline acceptance test.
